memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Our lives for your lives!" the men assured her. "If you don't tell what we are doing, we will treat you kindly and faithfully when the Lord gives us the land." — Josh 2:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The spies make Rahab a solemn promise: "Our lives for your lives!" It is a covenant, a binding pledge. They stake their own safety on keeping their word to her. What a beautiful picture of committed faithfulness — they will treat her "kindly and faithfully," the very words the Old Testament uses for God's own steadfast love.

Notice the exchange at the heart of this promise: our lives for your lives. One life offered so that another may be spared. If that phrase stirs something in you, it should. It quietly points forward to the greatest exchange of all.

For this is exactly what Jesus did for us. He said, "the Son of Man came... to give his life as a ransom for many" (Mark 10:45). His life for our lives. The spies pledged to protect Rahab if she trusted them; Christ actually laid down His life to save all who trust Him. Their promise cost them a risk; His promise cost Him everything.

There is also a lesson in keeping our word. The spies bound themselves to a promise and would honour it at real cost. In a world where promises are broken cheaply, God's people are called to be faithful — to let our yes be yes (Matt 5:37), reflecting the God who always keeps His covenant.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does the phrase "our lives for your lives" point you to Christ's sacrifice?
2. Are you someone whose promises can be trusted, even when keeping them is costly?
3. Have you personally received the exchange Jesus offers — His life for yours?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for giving Your life for mine. Help me trust Your promise fully, and make me faithful to keep my own word to others. Amen.
